title: PR body item 4 still claims 'demolished terminals free the budget' as delivered behavior, contradicting its own r1-fold W2 acknowledgment
evidence:
PR body item 4: "4. **District caps**: `cap(d) = max(1, floor(pool_tiles(d) × permille /
   1000))`, gating BOTH families; demolished terminals free the budget
   (live counts derive from the topology)." vs the r1-fold section: "**W2: demolish-frees-budget acknowledged vacuous-by-design** — E2 forbids
  terminal demolish (validate_demolish_node → .Terminal_Demolish), so the
  live count is monotone within a run; the spec/PR/balance comments now
  say so instead of claiming verified behavior."
detail: The claimed W2 disposition ('the PR comments now say so') is half-done: the PR's main director description still asserts the vacuous clause as verified behavior, so the document contradicts itself.
recommended_fix: Amend PR body item 4 to the vacuous-by-design wording already used in the r1-fold section and spec §1.4 (or delete the clause).

title: growth_districts tunables still parse via lenient jint — decimals silently truncate (r1 note unfixed despite the estate-spawning jint_strict precedent)
evidence:
b.growth_districts.district_cap_permille = jint(gobj, "district_cap_permille", -1)
			b.growth_districts.seed_weights[int(District_Kind.City)] = jint(gobj, "seed_weight_city", -1) [six jint rows] — while jint's body is: "case json.Float:   return i32(x)" (silent truncation) and the sibling block uses "seed_tiles, ok_seed := jint_strict(gobj, "new_area_seed_tiles", -1)".
detail: A decimal catalog value (e.g. seed_weight_city 4.5) loads silently as 4 — the exact ODN-10 trap growth_groups.new_area_seed_tiles was hardened against; the r1 note was not folded.
recommended_fix: Parse the seven growth_districts keys with jint_strict + a named load error (the new_area_seed_tiles precedent); add the decimal row to the fail-fast table.

title: District live counts still re-derived O(districts × nodes × anchors) per eligibility test — r1 note unfixed, the W1 fold added a third call site
evidence:
growth.odin:850-851: "d := map_district_assign(board, t.node_pos[i])
					if growth_district_live_count(board, t, d) >= growth_district_cap(board, cat, d) {" ; 565-566: "if growth_district_live_count(board, t, u16(d)) >= growth_district_cap(board, cat, u16(d)) {" (inside the per-district loop) ; live_count's body: "for i in 0..<len(t.node_alive) { ... if map_district_assign(board, t.node_pos[i]) == d {" — a full node scan (each node re-running the ≤52-anchor assign) per call.
detail: Every cap check re-scans all nodes; the seed-draw loop repeats it per district per attempt. r1 flagged this; the fold added another call instead of consolidating. Trivial at demo scale, quadratic in structure.
recommended_fix: Compute per-district live counts once per spawn window (one pass over nodes) and reuse for the cluster scan, SEED eligibility, and the W1 tile check.

title: W1 drawn-tile cap check calls map_district_assign twice for the same pos on one line (fold-introduced)
evidence: if growth_district_live_count(board, t, map_district_assign(board, pos)) >= growth_district_cap(board, cat, map_district_assign(board, pos)) {
detail: The identical nearest-anchor scan runs twice for the drawn tile — pure fold-introduced duplication on the hot rejection path; a local would express it once.
recommended_fix: td := map_district_assign(board, pos); then pass td to both growth_district_live_count and growth_district_cap.

title: run_dublin_grown is the 5th hand-rolled Demo_Replay construction — the fold centralized map_board_partition but left (and extended) this copy pattern
detail: Five copies of the same copy loop; every new Demo field must be threaded in five places (growth_on/map_source already forced per-site edits). The new verb repeated the pattern instead of extracting it.
recommended_fix: Extract one demo_replay_from_demo(d: ^Demo) -> Demo_Replay builder (session + growth_on + map_source + the three copy loops) and use it at all five sites.

title: dublin-grown census re-derives the per-candidate district assignment instead of reading the load-time partition it exists to centralize
detail: district_tiles already IS this census (map_board_partition's one definition holds per-district candidate indices); re-walking 603 candidates × 52 anchors re-derives the partition in the very verb documenting it.
recommended_fix: for d in 0..<len(bd.districts) { kind_totals[int(bd.districts[d].kind)] += len(bd.district_tiles[d]) } — same output, O(districts).
